mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase above 0.4 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their prior month's levels by at least 0.25 percentage points each signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > prior+0.25% AND CPIAUCSL > prior+0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% from the prior month indicates a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < prior-1% AND HOUST < prior-1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) below 50,000 new jobs for three consecutive months signals insufficient labor market expansion to sustain wage growth and consumer demand, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate policy easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 3% YoY, the real policy rate is deeply negative, which incentivizes risk-taking and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: ultra-loose monetary policy with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered regimes, or the average return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.
